heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock the power of next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 (Image Generation) and Seedance 1.5 Pro (Video Generation) - advanced foundation models developed by ByteDance for high-quality visual content creation.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use a full-bleed dark editorial hero with the background image treated as a layered generative collage, not a single product mockup. Place the long headline and supporting copy in a left-anchored content column over the overlay, while the right side of the hero is dominated by a large visual montage of image outputs, video frames, waveform/timeline UI, and subtle dashboard panels. Add a prominent orange CTA, a muted logo proof strip below the copy, and floating pill chips around the collage. Keep the composition asymmetrical and premium, with soft-shadow cards, grid-line accents, and a gradient mesh/orb treatment to signal enterprise-grade AI production.

repetitionBreakers: Full-bleed dark hero with layered product collage and prominent logo band
Light trust strip immediately after hero for contrast and continuity
Tabs-with-preview for the combined product section to handle many features without a static grid
Alternating dark and light product blocks to separate image and video capabilities
Testimonial carousel to introduce motion and avoid another static card cluster
Centered pricing cards followed by a high-contrast final CTA strip
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro by ByteDance | AI Image & Video Generation
blueprint.metaDescription: Explore ByteDance’s Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro for high-quality AI image generation, AI video generation, multimodal editing, and production-ready visual creation.

sections.backgroundTreatment: dark full-bleed gradient with layered generative visual collage, floating capability chips, and a dominant horizontal logo proof band
sections.designNote: Make the hero content-first and continuity-led: headline answers what this is, subheadline clarifies who it is for, and the single CTA button says 'Get started'. Use a rich editorial collage on the right/top with Seedream image outputs and Seedance video stills, but keep copy clearly legible. Add a compact proof band of 3-6 recognisable logos under the CTA to satisfy warm-traffic continuity and early trust.

Immediate post-hero trust reinforcement using a clean static flex-wrap logo grid. Keep it restrained and premium, with 3-6 recognisable logos if available. If logo assets are weak or fewer than three, replace this with a slim metrics strip. This section should feel like a credibility pause before product explanation.

Use one combined product architecture section with tabs for Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro, because each has many features. The first tab should spotlight image generation with a preview panel and short feature list; the second tab should switch to video generation with motion stills, waveform/timeline cues, and audio-visual sync emphasis. Avoid a flat static card grid. Alternate background tone and inner panel treatment between the two tabs so adjacent states feel distinct.

Because logos are the primary proof type, this section should stay logo-led rather than testimonial-led. Present a second muted logo strip with a concise supporting line about enterprise evaluation and production readiness. If additional logos are not available, convert this into a compact proof strip with key evaluation metrics instead.

Since whyTechjockey is not provided, repurpose this slot as a capability/value bridge rather than a generic vendor-benefits block. Use 3-4 editorial cards that explain evaluation advantages: compare image vs video, multimodal control, production-ready output, and quick demo-based decision making. Keep it concise and visually expressive so it doesn't feel like filler.

With 5 testimonials available, use a carousel or a controlled spotlight layout rather than a fixed grid. Include quotes from creative director, video producer, art director, and marketing lead to reinforce relevance. Keep the visuals minimal and editorial so the section feels like credible peer validation, not a marketing wall.

Present the two plans as centered premium cards with the image product slightly elevated if needed. Keep copy sparse and decision-oriented. The CTA on every card must be 'Get started'. Use solid accent buttons only, never outlined or gray. This is the first explicit conversion block after proof.

Replace the empty form config with a focused final conversion card if necessary: headline, short reassurance line, and one full-width mobile CTA button labeled 'Get started'. Keep it low-friction and visually calm, emphasizing demo access over aggressive sign-up language.

Do not use marquee movement. End with a static horizontal logo strip or muted footer trust row, paired with the extras/footer area. This final zone should feel like a credibility close rather than another promotional section.

blueprint.designPersonality: Editorial, enterprise-ready, and visually intelligent. The page should feel like a premium AI lab for visual production: dark foundation, orange-led brand energy, structured content blocks, prominent client logos, hover-rich cards, and a dedicated video gallery that signals motion capability. Strong contrast, layered surfaces, and precise spacing should make the product feel trustworthy and production-grade rather than experimental.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use a cinematic product collage built from AI-generated visuals, UI shells, and motion stills: one cluster for Seedream 4.5 image output previews, another for Seedance 1.5 Pro video thumbnails with waveform overlays and timeline UI. Add a dedicated video gallery section with 3-6 thumbnail cards, each showing a frame still, duration badge, and play affordance. Keep logos prominent in a horizontal trust band above the fold and again in a muted proof strip mid-page. Use SVG for icons and logos, PNG for product/UI visuals, and JPEG for the hero visual area.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is long, so a smaller size keeps the hero clean and premium without awkward line breaks.

colours.colourReason: Brand colors are locked to Techjockey’s provided palette. Since the product must use a dark theme, the charcoal base comes from the brand while the orange acts as the single primary accent and CTA color.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Split-feel above-the-fold banner with brand/logo area, large headline, short supporting copy, and a compact bullet list of key benefits. Primary CTA is visually emphasized; secondary CTA is absent or de-emphasized. Hero content is text-forward rather than media-led.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Single-column narrative flow with a strong hero, followed by stacked content blocks and a lead-generation form area. Sections are separated by clear vertical spacing and mild contrast changes rather than heavy decorative dividers.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Simple rectangular content cards with minimal ornamentation, light borders or subtle shadow, generous inner padding, and icon-optional feature rows. The style leans toward utility and clarity over glossy or glassmorphism effects.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: One dominant primary CTA per major section, repeated sparingly. CTA language is action-oriented and conversion-focused. Secondary CTAs, if present, are low-emphasis and not used as equal competitors to the primary action.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No pricing module present; the page pattern favors enterprise inquiry or demo-request conversion instead of plan comparison.
referenceMap.footerMode: Footer is not visible in the provided reference; likely a minimal utility/footer treatment rather than a content-rich sitemap footer.
spacingScale: sm: 12-16px for list spacing and inline grouping
md: 20-24px for card padding and section inner spacing
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Media usage is sparse or optional in the provided structure. The layout prioritizes text hierarchy, bullets, and form conversion over large image, video, or carousel media blocks.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Stacked feature sections, each beginning with a small label/kicker, followed by a strong headline, explanatory paragraph, and a feature list. Product areas are likely separated into distinct modules with repeated structure for comparison and easy scanning.
referenceMap.formPattern: Lead-capture form appears as a dedicated conversion block after the hero. Form card uses a headline, structured fields, and hidden tracking inputs. The form is treated as a primary conversion endpoint and visually boxed off from surrounding content.
referenceMap.animationStyle: No prominent motion system is evident in the reference. Interaction design appears static and conversion-oriented, with emphasis on clarity over animation.
componentPatterns: Hero headline with short supporting copy
Benefit bullet list with check icons
designNotes: Prioritize scannability with strong typographic hierarchy and short, benefit-led bullets.
Use one clear conversion path per screen area to reduce decision friction.
Keep module structure repeatable for multiple products or feature families.
Use contrast and spacing to separate sections instead of decorative complexity.
Treat forms as a prominent conversion component rather than a subtle sidebar element.

designStrategy.reasoning: This page is for professionals evaluating advanced AI image and video generation tools, so the best converting structure is product-led with enterprise-style reassurance. Because the user specifically said visitors trust logos most, trust should be built primarily through a prominent logo-first strip near the top and repeated subtle proof points later. The page should feel premium, technically credible, and easy to scan, with a split hero that foregrounds the value proposition and a dark theme that suits creative AI positioning. Since the goal is inquiry/demo booking rather than immediate self-serve purchase, the CTA strategy should stay assertive but not aggressive, with repeated quote/demo prompts across the page. A video gallery is important to prove Seedance capabilities visually and increase perceived quality.
